R924.summary: A writer at Paris to Charles I against Sir H. Compton's journey and the treaty for Prince Charles's marriage with Portugal, on Montreuil's mission, the frost that stopped the river traffic, and levies of five or six thousand men to send over.

Paris, 26 January. [207].

May it please your Majesty, you have so much [797] [320] hands that I will not begin another with you; but I lay it
down for the same reason that the [734]s continue theirs, that I am certainly too strong in the reasons on my side,
which I will briefly put to your Majesty.

First, though your Majesty should know that you are obeyed and Sir H. Compton is [487]ed, that there has been cause
for keeping him back is [231]; for his [151]ing, I mean the first [688] to send him, I allow that to be a good cause for
his [?himing];

system: Lasry's 'TNA SP106-8' key (Jan 1646): a numerical homophonic alphabet of one- and two-digit values (up to four for a vowel) with a numbered word list from 100 up (100 all, 101 are, 108 and, 141 for, 173 I, 174 in, 176 ing ...), numbers separated by colons.
